carmen: Noticed a small but reproducible set of SSE resumes where clients get accepted, then quickly see duplicated events + out-of-order seqs. Started after the pre-accept + rotate-on-fallback change. :thinking:

carmen: Example log:
```
[2026-08-02T12:22:10Z] conn=cid-218 resume=rt:xyZ tenant=atlas proxy=px-eu accept key=key-v1
[2026-08-02T12:22:10Z] route: initial_hint=pool-alpha final_choice=pool-gamma (fallback)
[2026-08-02T12:22:10Z] backend=shard-gamma replay_expected=780 replay_seen=11 -> seq_mismatch
[2026-08-02T12:22:10Z] emit duplicate_event id=evt_12a
```

diego: That looks like we accept before the final routing decision and prefetch a KV window tied to the initial pool. If final_choice differs, the prefetched window is invalid and we get mixed seqs.

rachel: We used pre-accept to shave off ~10ms for common resumes. The race shows up when fallback changes pool after accept. Rate ~0.8% for busy tenants. Customers flagged duplicate charges on per-route bills.

viktor: Two quick fixes: 1) move routing before accept (adds latency) or 2) keep accept but validate token.pool_ns == final_pool_ns before handing off cached KV. If mismatch, reject the resume and force cold reconnect.

carmen: I'd prefer option 2 as a rollback-friendly change. Add metric resume.pool_ns_mismatch{region,pool} and trace tag resume.hint_pool + resume.final_pool.

diego: Agree. Also emit trace span when we prefetch KV: `prefetch.shard_hint=...` so we can correlate prefetch vs final route.

rachel: UX: console currently shows resume_accept / resume_reject. We need a `resume.pool_mismatch` series and a small "deduped resumes" annotation on per-route billing so support can explain charges. Add a quick filter `pool_mismatch=true` in the transaction explorer.

viktor: Long-term: bake pool_ns and route_version into resume tokens so acceptance is deterministic. Also consider a soft-accept TTL where token is acceptable across route_version bump <=1.

ops-bot: playbook -> https://deploy.internal/redwood/playbooks/1840007777

carmen: Rollout plan: implement validation + metric behind flag; canary 2% eu for 4 hours, then 10% if stable. If duplicate rate drops, ramp. If not, revert to strict affinity.

diego: I'll PR the validation and metric today, will include the trace tags.

rachel: I'll scope console changes and a backfill job to mark deduped events for 72h via event-id matching.

viktor: I'll draft the token-format RFC and a migration plan for route_version compatibility.

carmen: Thanks 1— keep pasting any raw event ids or odd logs here during canary.
